name: FIN1019MTCX
title: 3.3 V LVDS differential line driver and receiver
summary: FIN1019 pairs one LVDS line driver with one LVDS line receiver in a 14-pin TSSOP running from 3.0 V to 3.6 V. The driver gives a 350 mV typical differential swing into 100 Ω; the receiver resolves 100 mV and holds its output HIGH when its inputs are open, shorted or terminated. Each half has its own enable, and with the supply off the driver outputs and all inputs pass no more than ±20 µA. Data rates run above 400 Mbps.
key_figures: 250 to 450 mV, 350 mV typ, RL = 100 Ω

pins.name: DE
pins.function: Driver enable, LVTTL level. HIGH turns the LVDS driver on; LOW puts DOUT+ and DOUT− in high impedance.

pins.name: ROUT
pins.function: Receiver data output, LVTTL level; high impedance while RE is HIGH.

pins.name: RE
pins.function: Receiver enable, LVTTL level, active LOW. LOW turns the receiver output on.

equations.name: Driver differential output
equations.note: Driver rise and fall are measured on VDIFF from 20% to 80% of the swing between −VOD and +VOD.

operation.text: One LVDS line driver and one LVDS line receiver on a single 3.3 V supply. The driver turns an LVTTL input into an LVDS pair with a typical 350 mV differential swing; the receiver turns an LVDS pair into an LVTTL output and switches on a differential input of 100 mV. Both meet or exceed TIA/EIA-644. Data rates go beyond 400 Mbps.

Into 100 Ω the differential output is 250 mV to 450 mV (350 mV typical), centred on an offset voltage of 1.125 V to 1.375 V (1.25 V typical). Neither the swing nor the offset shifts by more than 25 mV between the two output states. A shorted output sources no more than 8 mA. With DIN open or high impedance and DE HIGH, DOUT+ sits LOW and DOUT− HIGH.

ROUT is HIGH for a differential input above +100 mV and LOW below −100 mV, across a common-mode input range of 0.05 V to 2.35 V. The output swings to within 0.2 V of the rails at 100 µA and reaches 2.4 V high or 0.5 V low at 8 mA.
With the receiver enabled, ROUT goes HIGH when the inputs are left open, shorted together, or terminated.

DE is active HIGH and turns on the driver; RE is active LOW and turns on the receiver. A disabled output is high impedance and leaks no more than ±20 µA. Driver outputs enable or disable within 5.0 ns, and so does the receiver output.
With VCC = 0 V the driver outputs, the receiver inputs and the LVTTL inputs each pass no more than ±20 µA at 0 V or 3.6 V.
ICC is at most 12.5 mA with the driver on into 100 Ω, and at most 7.0 mA with the driver off.
Flow-through pinout: the LVTTL signals DE, DIN and ROUT are on pins 1, 2 and 4, and the LVDS pins on 9 to 12 along the opposite side, for a simpler board layout.
The top of the package carries the logo, an assembly plant code, a two-digit date code and a two-digit lot traceability code, with the device code FIN 1019.

TSSOP-14, case 948G: body 5.00 mm by 4.40 mm, 0.95 mm nominal body thickness, 0.65 mm pitch. D excludes mold flash, protrusions and gate burrs, up to 0.15 mm per side; E1 excludes interlead flash, up to 0.25 mm per side; b excludes dambar protrusion, up to 0.08 mm in total beyond b at maximum material. Recommended land pattern: 14 pads of 1.26 mm by 0.36 mm at 0.65 mm pitch, 7.06 mm across the outer pad ends. The part is lead-free, halide-free and RoHS compliant.
